scope: FIRST independent English scientific/Chinese-English fidelity, conditions/units/equations/source identity, and actual saved paragraph-flow readability only.
method: Read the entire actual English draft and all 28 saved paragraphs against all 10 exact approved Chinese blocks. Read-only file-byte, source-identity and paragraph-to-block comparisons bind the observations; counts and native token checks are not semantic proof. D004/D1156 science is reused, not re-solved. blockCoverage.observation: Constant stiffness and mass, Hooke's law, negligible spring mass and resistance precede the coefficient statement. Opposite acceleration/displacement directions and the magnitude k/m are retained. The last saved paragraph explicitly distinguishes natural angular frequency, the rate of phase change, from oscillations per second.

omega_0=sqrt(k/m), (1.23), is labelled natural angular frequency, not ordinary cyclic frequency. k and m retain stiffness/mass meanings. Newtons per meter, kilograms and radians per second are preserved and the unit paragraph follows the formula rather than preceding its symbol definitions.

Fixed mass and fixed stiffness separately qualify the comparisons. Same-displacement spring-force comparison and same-force mass comparison are retained. T=2 pi sqrt(m/k), (1.24), and seconds under the stated SI units are preserved. The paragraph sequence carries these qualifications without turning them into an unrestricted multi-parameter claim.

The experiment can test the stated parameter relations while separately controlling mass or stiffness and staying within Hooke's-law range. Resistance and other effects remain excluded from the parameter comparison. This is retained explanatory prose, not a newly added exercise or task.

Small-angle motion, point-mass bob, light inextensible taut string, fixed suspension, vertical plane, negligible drag/friction and approximately constant local g are retained before the formulas. l remains the suspension-to-center-of-mass distance. omega_0=sqrt(g/l), (1.25), and T=2 pi sqrt(l/g), (1.26), are explicitly approximate, with meters, meters per second squared, radians per second and seconds preserved. The final paragraph excludes arbitrary swing angles and arbitrary rigid pendulums. Saved paragraphs keep the prerequisite/model/formula/warning order.

Huygens, Dutch identity and contemporary-of-Newton relationship faithfully translate the approved Chinese. Priority and experimental confirmation are explicitly attributed to the original textbook's historical account. No new Huygens biography, priority determination or empirical verification is claimed.

Longer length, mass independence and smaller g are restricted to the same small-angle model and other conditions. Clock slowing requires unchanged other timing factors. Moscow University, ground-to-top-floor height increase of 200 meters, nearly 3 seconds lost per day, and the textbook's altitude explanation are retained as a historical approximate example. The continuation distinguishes a rod-and-weight clock from an ideal simple pendulum and excludes universal exact predictions. No new measurement or building verification was performed.

Gravity inference needs measured period and calibrated pendulum length; precision depends on timing, length and control of finite-angle/resistance effects. Latitude and same-latitude differences remain separated. Density contrast, not ore hardness, is the relevant property. Gravity anomalies are clues, not a unique determination of mineral type or burial location. The saved three-paragraph progression preserves the inverse-measurement limitations.

A. A. Mikhailov, Soviet Academy of Sciences, Kursk, iron ore, and prior magnetic indications remain in a source-attributed historical exploration account. Measurements clarify earlier indicated locations rather than independently identifying iron ore without conditions. The second paragraph retains complementarity and the restriction. No fresh historical verification is asserted.

Amplitude independence is exact only for the ideal linear spring model and approximate for small-angle pendulum motion. Same initial phase and scaling of BOTH initial displacement and initial velocity precede doubling of force, acceleration and velocity at corresponding times. Twice the distance in the same time and unchanged period are retained. The conclusion rejects a general arbitrary-initial-condition acceleration-to-velocity scaling rule and repeats the pendulum's small-angle limitation.
